class User < ApplicationRecord
  ROLES = %w[admin agent customer].freeze
  STAFF_ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  EMAIL_FORMAT = /\A[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+\z/
  MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8

  belongs_to :account
  has_many :sessions, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :user_tokens, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :requested_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :requester_id, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :requester
  has_many :assigned_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :assignee_id, dependent: :nullify, inverse_of: :assignee
  has_many :comments, foreign_key: :author_id, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :author
  has_many :sent_invitations, class_name: "Invitation", foreign_key: :invited_by_id, dependent: :nullify, inverse_of: :invited_by
  has_many :accepted_invitations, class_name: "Invitation", foreign_key: :accepted_user_id, dependent: :nullify, inverse_of: :accepted_user

  has_secure_password

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.strip }
  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :email,
    presence: true,
    format: { with: EMAIL_FORMAT },
    uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: ROLES }
  validates :suspended, inclusion: { in: [ true, false ] }
  validates :password, length: { minimum: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH }, if: -> { password.present? }

  before_save :sync_suspended_at

  scope :active, -> { where(suspended: false) }
  scope :suspended_only, -> { where(suspended: true) }
  scope :staff, -> { where(role: STAFF_ROLES) }
  scope :active_staff, -> { staff.active }
  scope :active_admins, -> { where(role: "admin", suspended: false) }
  scope :ordered_by_id, -> { order(id: :asc) }

  def verified?
    email_verified_at.present?
  end

  def active?
    !suspended?
  end

  def admin?
    role == "admin"
  end

  def agent?
    role == "agent"
  end

  def customer?
    role == "customer"
  end

  def staff?
    admin? || agent?
  end

  def owner?
    account.owner?(self)
  end

  def verify_email!

    class UsersController < BaseController
      before_action :resolve_account!
      before_action :authenticate_user!
      before_action :require_active_account!
      before_action :require_admin!

      def index
        relation = current_account.users.ordered_by_id

        if params.key?(:role) && params[:role].to_s.strip != ""
          requested_role = params[:role].to_s.strip.downcase
          unless User::ROLES.include?(requested_role)
            render json: {
              error: "Role is not included in the list",
              errors: { role: [ "is not included in the list" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_content
            return
          end
          relation = relation.where(role: requested_role)
        end

        if params.key?(:suspended) && params[:suspended].to_s.strip != ""
          raw_suspended = params[:suspended].to_s.strip.downcase
          case raw_suspended
          when "true"
            relation = relation.where(suspended: true)
          when "false"
            relation = relation.where(suspended: false)
          else
            render json: {
              error: "Suspended must be true or false",
              errors: { suspended: [ "must be true or false" ] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_content
            return
          end
        end

        result = paginate(relation)

        render json: {
          users: result[:records].map { |user| serialize_user(user) }
        }.merge(result[:meta]), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        user = current_account.users.find(params[:id])
        render json: { user: serialize_user(user) }, status: :ok
      end

      def update
        user_envelope = require_object_param(:user)

        user = nil
        updated = false

        current_account.with_lock do
          user = current_account.users.find(params[:id])

          if user_envelope.key?(:name)
            user.assign_attributes(user_envelope.permit(:name))
          end

          suspended_invalid = false
          requested_suspended = nil
          if user_envelope.key?(:suspended)
            raw_suspended = user_envelope[:suspended]
            if [ true, false ].include?(raw_suspended)
              requested_suspended = raw_suspended
              user.suspended = raw_suspended
            else
              suspended_invalid = true
            end
          end

          user_valid = user.valid?
          if suspended_invalid
            user.errors.add(:suspended, "must be a boolean")
            user_valid = false
          end

          if requested_suspended == true && user.admin?
            other_active_admins = current_account.users.active_admins.where.not(id: user.id).exists?
            unless other_active_admins
              user.errors.add(:suspended, "cannot suspend the last active admin")
              user_valid = false
            end
          end

          if user_valid
            user.save!
            if user.suspended?
              user.revoke_all_sessions!
              user.clear_assigned_tickets!
            end
            updated = true
          end
        end

        unless updated
          render_validation_errors(user)
          return
        end

        render json: { user: serialize_user(user) }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end

steps.reasoning_content:
**Analyzing Staff Ticket Filtering and Search Requirements**

Okay, here's the breakdown, starting with a review of a crucial Rails pattern. It seems internal attributes, like `public` on a ticket, are ignored by design when sent through customer endpoints, which is smart. Moving on, I've got to carefully consider the filtering and search requirements for the staff ticket list endpoint (`GET /api/v1/tickets`). I need to analyze every single filter parameter, including valid, invalid, blank, and edge cases. I'm seeing a common filtering pattern within the codebase that needs to be followed closely.

*   **Common Pattern:** I'm seeing that missing, blank, or whitespace-only filter parameters are ignored. This is the behavior of existing controller index actions. Non-string params are invalid, and I need to handle multi-invalid filter params by returning all errors in a single 422 response. The error response format must match existing behavior.

Now, into the specifics of each parameter.

*   **Status (`status`):** Valid values are "open," "pending," and "solved," and I'll make sure it's case-insensitive and stripped of whitespace before comparison. I need to reject non-string values. If an invalid string is sent, the API must return a 422 with a specific error message.

*   **Priority (`priority`):** For this one, valid values are "normal" and "high", it's only for the staff endpoint, and blank/omitted will mean no filter. The handling is the same as the `status` param, stripping and lowercasing with a similar 422 response for an invalid value.

*   **Assignee ID (`assignee_id`):** This is where it gets tricky. Valid values are "unassigned" (case-insensitive), or a positive integer ID. Blank or omitted is no filter. Invalid inputs like "abc," "0," negative numbers, floating points, or arrays will need to return a 422. I need to think carefully about how to treat a valid ID that doesn't exist. I'm leaning toward a 200 OK with an empty result set (since the tickets are scoped to the current account) instead of 422 for a non-existent ID. I also need to make sure to account for integer overflow (Postgres' bigint range) to avoid `ActiveModel::RangeError`. Invalid ID inputs like non-integers, `"0"`, `"-1"` must be a 422.

*   **Requester ID (`requester_id`):** Similar to `assignee_id`, this filter accepts a positive integer ID. But I have to note that a ticket must always have a requester. "Unassigned" will always return a 422 because every ticket needs a requester. Invalid values (non-integers) must get a 422.

*   **Search Query (`q`):** This one needs extra care. The requirement is to perform a case-insensitive, literal text search through subjects and public comments only. Private notes are excluded. The prompt is very specific about treating the input as literal text. I need to handle SQL LIKE metacharacters (`%`, `_`, `\`) properly by escaping them. The absence, emptiness, or whitespace-only `q` should mean no filter. A non-string value for `q` has to be rejected with 422.

The key considerations here for the search are:

1.  **Field Specificity:** The search must only be on ticket subjects and public comments. Private notes must be ignored.
2.  **Literal Text:** "Literal" means I need to make sure that the SQL LIKE wildcards (% and \_) are escaped properly. This includes backslashes and special characters (with `ESCAPE '\'`). I'll use `ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like` which will escape `\` `%` and `_` with a `\`
3.  **Whitespace:** Blank or whitespace-only `q` means no search. Stripping whitespace from a non-empty `q` seems consistent with the API.
4.  **Non-String:** Only strings will be considered valid search query terms.

That covers every edge case and requirement. Now I can translate these requirements into robust and consistent code!

cd /app && bin/rails runner '
  conn = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
  puts "PG version: #{conn.select_value("SELECT version()")}"
  puts "Encoding: #{conn.select_value("SHOW server_encoding")}"
  puts "LC_CTYPE: #{conn.select_value("SHOW lc_ctype")}"
  puts "LC_COLLATE: #{conn.select_value("SHOW lc_collate")}"
  puts "standard_conforming_strings: #{conn.select_value("SHOW standard_conforming_strings")}"

  # Test sanitize_sql_like with %, _, \, quotes, regex chars, unicode
  [
    ["100% off", "100%", true],
    ["1000 off", "100%", false],
    ["order_123", "order_123", true],
    ["orderX123", "order_123", false],
    ["C:\\Users\\test", "\\", true],
    ["C:/Users/test", "\\", false],
    ["100\\% literal", "\\%", true],
    ["100% literal", "\\%", false],
    ["foo.*bar", ".*", true],
    ["fooxxxbar", ".*", false],
    ["Café receipt", "café", true],
    ["Receipt", "RECEIPT", true],
    ["O'\''Brien", "o'\''brien", true]
  ].each do |haystack, needle, expected|
    pattern = "%#{ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like(needle)}%"
    sql = ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_array(["SELECT ? ILIKE ? ESCAPE '\''\\\\'\''", haystack, pattern])
    actual = conn.select_value(sql)
    puts "#{actual == expected ? "OK" : "FAIL"}: haystack=#{haystack.inspect} needle=#{needle.inspect} expected=#{expected} actual=#{actual}"
  end
'

  scope :recently_active_for_customer, -> { order(customer_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :for_requester, ->(user) { where(requester_id: user.id) }
  scope :with_status, ->(status) { where(status: status) }
  scope :with_priority, ->(priority) { where(priority: priority) }

    where(<<~'SQL', pattern: pattern)

      OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM comments
        WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id

          AND comments.public = TRUE

  test "search q treats SQL LIKE wildcards, backslashes, regex chars, quotes, and special text strictly literally" do
    signup_and_verify!(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test")
    owner_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test")["session"]["token"]

    avery_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password")["session"]["token"]

    create_req = lambda do |subject, body|
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: subject, comment: { body: body } } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :created
      json_body["request"]["id"]
    end

    t_pct = create_req.call("100% refund requested", "Expecting 100% back")
    t_num = create_req.call("1000 credits issue", "Missing 1000 credits")
    t_under = create_req.call("Failed order_123", "Reference order_123")
    t_non_under = create_req.call("Failed orderX123", "Reference orderX123")
    t_slash = create_req.call("Windows path error", 'File at C:\Users\Avery\100\%_test.txt')
    t_regex = create_req.call("Regex literal test", "Pattern foo.*bar [urgent] (v1+v2)? $9.99")
    t_regex_other = create_req.call("Other pattern", "Pattern fooXXXbar urgent v1v2 999")
    t_quote = create_req.call("O'Brien billing", "Café invoice -- not SQL ' OR 1=1 --")
    t_phrase = create_req.call("Cannot download file", "Cannot see download button")

    # Add a private note containing all special literals on t_num to verify private notes never match
    patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t_num}",
      params: { ticket: { comment: { body: '100% order_123 C:\Users foo.*bar CAFÉ', public: false } } },
      headers: account_headers("acme", token: owner_token),
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    assert_search = lambda do |term, expected_ids|
      get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: term }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: owner_token)
      assert_response :ok, "Search failed for q=#{term.inspect}"
      assert_equal expected_ids.sort, json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }.sort,
        "Unexpected results for q=#{term.inspect}"
    end

    assert_search.call("100%", [ t_pct ])
    assert_search.call("%", [ t_pct, t_slash ])
    assert_search.call("order_123", [ t_under ])
    assert_search.call("_", [ t_under, t_slash ])
    assert_search.call('\\', [ t_slash ])
    assert_search.call('c:\users\avery', [ t_slash ])
    assert_search.call('\\%', [ t_slash ])
    assert_search.call("foo.*bar", [ t_regex ])
    assert_search.call("[urgent]", [ t_regex ])
    assert_search.call("(v1+v2)?", [ t_regex ])
    assert_search.call("$9.99", [ t_regex ])
    assert_search.call("o'brien", [ t_quote ])
    assert_search.call("' OR 1=1 --", [ t_quote ])
    assert_search.call("CAFÉ", [ t_quote ])
    assert_search.call("cannot download", [ t_phrase ])
    assert_search.call("cannot button", [])
    assert_search.call("  100%  ", [ t_pct ])

    # NUL byte returns empty 200 safely without crashing
    get "/api/v1/tickets?q=abc%00def", headers: account_headers("acme", token: owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [], json_body["tickets"]
    assert_equal 0, json_body["count"]
  end

  test "customers can filter their own requests by status with pagination, isolation, and no internal priority leakage" do
    signup_and_verify!(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test")
    owner_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test")["session"]["token"]

    avery_id = register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test")["user"]["id"]
    blake_id = register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Blake", email: "blake@example.test")["user"]["id"]
    avery_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password")["session"]["token"]
    blake_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "blake@example.test", password: "my-customer-password")["session"]["token"]

    base = Time.zone.parse("2026-09-01 09:00:00 UTC")
    ids = {}

    [
      [ :a_open_1, avery_token, "Avery open 1" ],
      [ :a_pending, avery_token, "Avery pending" ],
      [ :a_solved, avery_token, "Avery solved" ],
      [ :a_open_2, avery_token, "Avery open 2" ],
      [ :b_open, blake_token, "Blake open" ]
    ].each_with_index do |(key, tok, subject), idx|
      travel_to base + idx.minutes do
        post "/api/v1/requests",
          params: { request: { subject: subject, comment: { body: "Body for #{subject}" } } },
          headers: account_headers("acme", token: tok),
          as: :json
        assert_response :created
        ids[key] = json_body["request"]["id"]
      end
    end

    # Staff sets statuses and priorities
    travel_to base + 10.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ids[:a_pending]}",
        params: { ticket: { status: "pending", priority: "high" } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", token: owner_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    travel_to base + 11.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ids[:a_solved]}",
        params: { ticket: { status: "solved", priority: "high" } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", token: owner_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    travel_to base + 12.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{ids[:a_open_1]}",
        params: { ticket: { priority: "high" } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", token: owner_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # Customer filters own requests by status (ordered by customer_updated_at desc; a_open_1 priority change did NOT bump it above a_open_2!)
    get "/api/v1/requests?status=open", headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ ids[:a_open_2], ids[:a_open_1] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]
    json_body["requests"].each { |r| assert_not r.key?("priority") }

    get "/api/v1/requests?status=pending", headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ ids[:a_pending] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]

    get "/api/v1/requests?status=SOLVED", headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ ids[:a_solved] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]

    # Pagination with status filter
    get "/api/v1/requests?status=open&page=1&per_page=1", headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ ids[:a_open_2] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal 2, json_body["next_page"]
    assert_nil json_body["previous_page"]

    # Blank status returns all of Avery's requests (never Blake's)
    get "/api/v1/requests?status=", headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]
    assert_not_includes json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }, ids[:b_open]

    # Internal/staff filters (priority, assignee_id, requester_id, q) are ignored on customer /requests endpoint
    get "/api/v1/requests?priority=high", headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]

    get "/api/v1/requests?status=open&priority=high&requester_id=#{blake_id}&q=open%201",
      headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ ids[:a_open_2], ids[:a_open_1] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]

    # Blake sees only Blake's own requests when filtering by status
    get "/api/v1/requests?status=open", headers: account_headers("acme", token: blake_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ ids[:b_open] ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]

    get "/api/v1/requests?status=solved", headers: account_headers("acme", token: blake_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [], json_body["requests"]
    assert_equal 0, json_body["count"]

    # Invalid status on /requests returns 422
    [ "status=closed", "status=bogus", "status[]=open" ].each do |query|
      get "/api/v1/requests?#{query}", headers: account_headers("acme", token: avery_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content, "Expected 422 for /requests?#{query}"
      assert json_body["errors"]["status"].present?
    end
  end
end

    where(<<~'SQL', pattern: pattern)

        WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id

          AND comments.public = TRUE
          AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\'

    now = current_time_from_proper_timezone
    self.created_at ||= now

steps.message: I'll run a quick end-to-end HTTP smoke test against Puma using real `curl` requests (including URL-encoded literal search queries) and clean up afterward.
steps.reasoning_content:
Okay, here's my interpretation of that thought process, tailored for an expert audience:

**Smoke Testing Puma in a Production-Like Environment**

Alright, the objective is straightforward: achieve a high level of confidence in our Puma instance. We're going to kick off a live smoke test. We'll direct this test at `http://127.0.0.1:3099`, a local address for our test Puma process. This implies that we're mimicking a production-like environment with this configuration.

The crucial part is ensuring real HTTP requests are handled correctly. We aren't just verifying boot; we are verifying a live response to live HTTP traffic.

Following the successful test, we need a complete cleanup. We'll be removing any database records that the test creates to ensure a clean state after the verification, and finally, stopping Puma. This is essential to prevent any potential resource conflicts or lingering processes after the test. This entire approach suggests a careful and methodical approach to validating our setup before deploying into a live setting. It's about minimizing risk and ensuring reliability.

arguments.command:
cd /app && bash -e -c '
  bin/rails server -p 3099 -b 127.0.0.1 -P tmp/pids/smoke.pid >/tmp/smoke_puma.log 2>&1 &
  SERVER_PID=$!
  trap "kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true; wait $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true; rm -f tmp/pids/smoke.pid /tmp/smoke_puma.log" EXIT

  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3099/up >/dev/null; then
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.2
  done

  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3099/up >/dev/null
  echo "Server is up!"

  # Run ruby Net::HTTP smoke test against real Puma server and clean up DB records in ensure
  bin/rails runner '\''
    require "net/http"
    require "json"
    require "uri"

    def req(method, path, headers: {}, body: nil)
      uri = URI("http://127.0.0.1:3099#{path}")
      http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port)
      klass = { get: Net::HTTP::Get, post: Net::HTTP::Post, patch: Net::HTTP::Patch }[method]
      r = klass.new(uri.request_uri, headers)
      if body
        r["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
        r.body = JSON.generate(body)
      end
      res = http.request(r)
      [res.code.to_i, JSON.parse(res.body)]
    end

    account = Account.create!(name: "SmokeCo", subdomain: "smokeco")
    begin
      admin = account.users.create!(name: "Admin", email: "admin@smoke.test", password: "password123", role: "admin", email_verified_at: Time.current)
      account.update!(owner: admin)
      cust = account.users.create!(name: "Cust", email: "cust@smoke.test", password: "password123", role: "customer", email_verified_at: Time.current)

      code, admin_sess = req(:post, "/api/v1/sessions", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "smokeco" }, body: { session: { email: "admin@smoke.test", password: "password123" } })
      raise "admin login failed: #{code}" unless code == 201
      admin_hdr = { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "smokeco", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{admin_sess["session"]["token"]}" }

      code, cust_sess = req(:post, "/api/v1/sessions", headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "smokeco" }, body: { session: { email: "cust@smoke.test", password: "password123" } })
      raise "cust login failed: #{code}" unless code == 201
      cust_hdr = { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "smokeco", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{cust_sess["session"]["token"]}" }

      code, r1 = req(:post, "/api/v1/requests", headers: cust_hdr, body: { request: { subject: "100% receipt missing", comment: { body: "Need invoice_42" } } })
      raise "create req failed: #{code}" unless code == 201 && !r1["request"].key?("priority")
      t1 = r1["request"]["id"]

      code, r2 = req(:post, "/api/v1/requests", headers: cust_hdr, body: { request: { subject: "1000 points", comment: { body: "Check invoiceX42" } } })
      raise "create req 2 failed: #{code}" unless code == 201
      t2 = r2["request"]["id"]

      code, u1 = req(:patch, "/api/v1/tickets/#{t1}", headers: admin_hdr, body: { ticket: { priority: "high" } })
      raise "update priority failed: #{code}" unless code == 200 && u1["ticket"]["priority"] == "high"

      code, list = req(:get, "/api/v1/tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=100%25", headers: admin_hdr)
      raise "filter failed: #{code} #{list}" unless code == 200 && list["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] } == [t1]

      code, cust_list = req(:get, "/api/v1/requests?status=open", headers: cust_hdr)
      raise "cust filter failed: #{code}" unless code == 200 && cust_list["count"] == 2 && !cust_list["requests"].first.key?("priority")

      puts "Live Puma HTTP smoke test PASSED!"
    ensure
      account.destroy
    end
  '\''
' && bin/rails test
